rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All prophets call people to worship God alone and warn against shirk or claims of divinity; the People of the Book are rebuked for imagining prophets could claim godhood and are urged to reconsider through their own scriptures and study.
rows.anchor: bütün peygamberlerin yalnız Allah’a kulluk etme çağrısıyla görevlendirildiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hukm lexically means deciding, governing, restraining, or preventing; philosophically it is an affirmative or negative relation between ideas or states and its apprehension, and it is classified by knowledge source and field.
rows.anchor: Sözlükte hüküm kelimesi “karar vermek, yönetmek, alıkoymak, engellemek” gibi anlamlara gelir.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says language and tafsir scholars agree that hukm here is the prophet's grasp of the revealed Book and the knowledge formed through that understanding.
rows.anchor: dil ve tefsir âlimlerinin bu âyette geçen hüküm kelimesiyle, Allah tarafından indirilen kitabın peygamber tarafından kavranmasının

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya explains hukm here as wisdom.
rows.anchor: Bazı müfessirler bunu “hikmet” (İbn Atıyye, I, 461)

rows.speaker: Muhammed Esed
rows.claim: Muhammad Asad renders hukm as sound judgment.
rows.anchor: “sağlam muhâkeme” (Muhammed Esed, I, 105)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses hukm of God for absolute will, sovereignty, and authority to decide, and of prophets or people for settling legal disputes.
rows.anchor: mutlak irade, hâkimiyet ve karar yetkisi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nubuwwa means prophethood; those assigned this office by God are called nabi (plural anbiya) and rasul (plural rusul).
rows.anchor: Nübüvvet “peygamberlik” demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One occasion report says the Prophet warned Quraysh against worshipping angels, Jews against Uzayr, and Christians against Jesus; they asked whether he wanted them to take him as lord, prompting revelation.
rows.anchor: Kureyş müşriklerini meleklere, yahudileri Üzeyir’e, hıristiyanları da Îsâ’ya kulluk etmekten sakındırıyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says a Muslim asked whether they could prostrate to the Prophet as a distinctive greeting, and the verses were revealed because of that request.
rows.anchor: Sana secde ederek farklı bir selâm versek olmaz mı?” dediği için bu âyetler indi.

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: From the statement that a prophet would not command disbelief after people became Muslims, Zamakhshari takes the addressees to be Muslims and considers the prostration-greeting report stronger.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî 80. âyette geçen “Siz müslüman olduktan sonra size inkârcılığı emreder mi hiç!” ifadesinden hareketle

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur considers it unlikely that the verse intends the interpretation that its addressees were Muslims responding to the greeting proposal.
rows.anchor: İbn Âşûr âyette bu mânanın kastedilmiş olabileceğine ihtimal vermez

rows.speaker: Muhammed Abduh
rows.claim: Abduh regards the prostration-greeting report as highly problematic for Qur'anic interpretation and contrary to the verse's flow of meaning.
rows.anchor: Muhammed Abduh bu rivayeti Kur’an’ın tefsiri açısından çok sakıncalı görür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning prophets as lords and angels as lords covers the highest creatures in the material and immaterial realms: worshipping anyone but God conflicts with divine religion, and no rational person can imagine a prophet teaching otherwise.
rows.anchor: hangi meziyetlere sahip olursa olsun Allah’tan başkasına kulluk etmenin ilâhî dinlerin ilkeleriyle bağdaşmayacağı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting saints, shaykhs, clergy, diviners, jinn, devils, or even irrational and inanimate things in God's place conflicts with the motive for worship; such substitutions are futile distractions and waste reason.
rows.anchor: Veli, şeyh, rahip, haham, kâhin, cin, şeytan vb. varlıkları rab yerine koyarak onlara bel bağlamak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship acquires meaning through sincere submission to God, creator of servants and the universe, whose existence and power depend on nothing; humans attain their true worth through this worship.
rows.anchor: “kul”luk ancak kulların ve bütün evrenin yaratıcısı olan, varlığı ve gücü başka hiçbir varlığa bağlı olmayan yüce Allah’a

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ibad rather than abid for abd signals that no object of worship besides God can promise or grant a person the status of being worshipped.
rows.anchor: abd kelimesinin abîd değil ibâd şeklindeki çoğulu kullanılarak Allah’tan başka hiçbir mâbudun insana bu mevkii vaad edemeyeceğine

rows.speaker: İbn Atıyye
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya finds that Qur'anic ibad occurs in contexts that honor the servant's will to obey, without connotations of pity or contempt.
rows.anchor: ibâdın “acıma ve küçümseme” anlamıyla ilişkili olmayan, kulun itaat iradesine dikkat çeken

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some commentators say the references to prophets and angels as lords condemn Jewish claims that Uzayr and Christian claims that Jesus was God's son, and the Christian Trinity, including the Holy Spirit.
rows.anchor: özellikle bazı yahudilerin Üzeyir’i ve hıristiyanların Îsâ’yı Allah’ın oğlu saymalarının

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur suggests the verse may allude to Christians making images of prophets and angels, venerating them excessively, and adopting practices resembling idolatry.
rows.anchor: hıristiyanların bazı peygamberlerin ve meleklerin resimlerini yapıp onları kutsama hususunda aşırı gitmelerine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophetic counsel is summarized as “Be rabbaniyyun.”
rows.anchor: Bir peygamberin neyi söylemesinin düşünülemeyeceği belirtildikten sonra, peygamberlerin tavsiyesi şu şekilde özetlenmiştir: “Rabbânîler olun!”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic etymologies explain rabbaniyyun as those who know their Lord and strive to worship Him, learned people who teach and urge good, or educators who train people and guide society; some scholars instead derive it from Syriac or Hebrew.
rows.anchor: “Rabb”ini bilen ve daima O’na kulluk etme çabası gösterenler

rows.speaker: Ömer Faruk Harman
rows.claim: In Hebrew, rab (rav) means great and later master or owner; rabbi means my master or teacher, and rabban is an intensified form; rabbaniyyun (rabbanim) are religious scholars, especially Torah scholars, who teach correct belief.
rows.anchor: Özetle İbrânîce’de rabbâniyyûn (rabbanîm), dinî ilimlerle ve bilhassa Tevrat’la meşgul olup halka doğru inanç öğreten din üstatları demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabbaniyyun occurs twice elsewhere beside ahbar, referring to Jewish scholars charged with preserving Torah rulings, teaching them, and ensuring Jews live by them.
rows.anchor: Rabbâniyyûn kelimesi Kur’an-ı Kerîm’in iki âyetinde daha “yahudi din bilginleri” anlamına gelen “ahbâr” kelimesiyle birlikte geçmekte

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Be rabbaniyyun” can call everyone to sincere worship of God or especially remind knowledge-bearers and social leaders to teach truth and guide people to salvation; the following reference to teaching and studying supports the latter reading.
rows.anchor: Bu öğütün “öğretmekte olduğunuz kitap ve yapmakta olduğunuz incelemeler gereğince” şeklinde bir dayanağa bağlanması ikinci anlamı teyit etmektedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When leaders truly dedicate themselves to God's path and recognize their duty, those needing guidance have no opening to elevate them to lordly status.
rows.anchor: bu sorumluluğun bilincinde olmaları halinde, yol gösterilmeye muhtaç kişilerin yukarıda değinilen çarpık telakkiye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse links knowledge to action: knowledge gains real value through practice, and people should avoid words and behavior that contradict what they have studied and taught.
rows.anchor: ilmin, ancak hayata yansıtılmakla ve aksiyon haline getirilmekle kuru bilgi olmaktan kurtulup gerçek değerini bulabileceği

rows.speaker: M. Reşîd Rızâ
rows.claim: Rashid Rida explains “after you became Muslims” as “according to human nature.”
rows.anchor: M. Reşîd Rızâ “fıtrat gereğince” şeklinde açıklar.

rows.speaker: Muhammed Abduh
rows.claim: Abduh says Jesus could not ask the People of the Book to worship him after they followed Moses and became monotheists; he criticizes readings that restrict the verse to Muslims, since Islam is the religion of all prophets and the religion of human nature.
rows.anchor: Kur’an ıstılahında İslâm’ın bütün peygamberlerin dini ve fıtrat dini olduğunu unuttukları eleştirisini yöneltir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant passage recalls the unity of all prophets' messages: each affirms earlier revelation, while earlier communities believe and support the next messenger, creating reciprocal testimony; this helps the People of the Book remain consistent and answer the call begun in 3:64.
rows.anchor: her peygamberin kendinden önceki ilâhî bildirimlerin doğruluğunu beyan etmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One main reading takes the covenant from the prophets themselves: they would believe and support a later messenger, either affirming one another generally or foretelling Muhammad.
rows.anchor: burada söz verenler peygamberlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other main reading is that the prophets' communities pledged to believe and support Muhammad when he came, rather than the prophets making the pledge themselves.
rows.anchor: burada kastedilen bizzat peygamberlerden söz alınması değil

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhshari narrows the community addressed to Israelites who regarded themselves as prophets' descendants or People of the Book who thought themselves more entitled to prophethood.
rows.anchor: kendilerini peygamberlerin çocukları sayan İsrâiloğulları’ndan veya kendilerini peygamberlik verilmeye daha lâyık gören Ehl-i kitap’tan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes use wording in Ubayy ibn Ka'b's and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud's personal codices to claim it is the Qur'anic text; the author says this exceeds interpretation and violates the Companions' consensus on the Uthmani codex, since such additions are explanatory notes.
rows.anchor: sahâbenin Mushaf-ı Osmânî üzerindeki icmâına aykırıdır

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Some scholars posit an additional clause about Book and wisdom: God took a pledge that recipients convey them and then believe and help a confirming messenger who comes.
rows.anchor: Allah peygamberlerden ‘Size verdiğim kitap ve hikmeti muhakkak insanlara tebliğ edecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators debate whether every prophet or every community received a Book: one view says every prophet was given a Book by following and summoning to one, though not all received one directly; another says all prophets are addressed by the superior trait of those given scripture.
rows.anchor: bütün peygamberlere kitap “indirilmemiş” olmakla beraber hepsine kitap “verilmiş”tir

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Book means revelation sent to and recited by a prophet, whereas wisdom is revelation about detailed rulings not included in the Book.
rows.anchor: Kitap peygambere indirilen ve okunan vahiydir. Hikmet ise kitabın içermediği ayrıntılı hükümlerle ilgili vahiydir

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: A later prophet, especially Muhammad, confirms predecessors because prophetic teachings share faith and moral foundations; even different teachings validate an earlier prophet if the later one says following the earlier revelation was then right and pleasing to God; Muhammad's coming also confirms Torah and Gospel since they foretold him.
rows.anchor: İlâhî dinlerin öğretileri inanç ve ahlâk esasları açısından aynı çizgide olduğu için

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi offers two readings of the covenant: God placed in prophets' minds proofs that obedience to His command is obligatory, or God described His attributes in earlier prophets' scriptures.
rows.anchor: Allah Teâlâ’nın, kendi emrine boyun eğmenin vâcip olduğunu gösteren delilleri peygamberlerin akıllarına yerleştirmesidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isr can mean burden, covenant, or bond; although used elsewhere for a burden, the surrounding context makes covenant the meaning here.
rows.anchor: ifadenin önü ve sonu dikkate alınarak burada kelimeye ahid mânası verilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant's question-and-answer exchange may represent dialogue between God and the prophets or between prophets and their communities, depending on which main interpretation is followed.
rows.anchor: ya Allah Teâlâ ile peygamberleri ya da peygamberlerle ümmetleri arasında geçen konuşmalar olarak düşünülmüştür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Bear witness” may mean the pledge-makers witness one another, angels witness the exchange, each person witnesses their own pledge as at the primordial covenant, the pledge is public to prevent ignorance claims, it ensures certainty, or communities are asked to testify.
rows.anchor: elest bezminde (bk. A‘râf 7/172) olduğu gibi herkesin kendi verdiği söze şahit olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's demand for witnesses does not meet any need of His, since He knows all; it highlights mutual testimony in the universe by His will and the requirement to prove accusations and responsibility, inviting reflection.
rows.anchor: böyle bir tanıklık talep etmesi kuşkusuz O’nun buna olan ihtiyacıyla açıklanamaz

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhshari says “I am with you among the witnesses” reinforces the pledge's binding force and warns against withdrawing from it.
rows.anchor: bu sözün bağlayıcılığına güç katmak ve bundan dönmekten sakındırmak içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribbiyyun means those attached to the Lord, worshipping God and following His religion; it is synonymous with rabbani and can mean followers or disciples of prophets.
rows.anchor: “Allah’a kulluk edenler, O’nun dinine uyanlar” demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribbiyyun is also explained as “the earlier ones” or, deriving it from ribb, as a community.
rows.anchor: “öncekiler” diye açıklandığı gibi, “ribbe” kelimesine nisbet edilerek “cemaat” anlamında da tefsir edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Elmalılı
rows.claim: Elmalili prefers deriving ribbiyyun from ribb, community, as an educated community, and rabbaniyyun from rabb, educator, as people advanced enough to teach and train them.
rows.anchor: ribbiyyûnu cemaat anlamına gelen “ribb”e nisbet ederek “eğitim görmüş cemaat”, rabbâniyyûnu ise

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes Muslims who fled after hearing that the Prophet had been killed: earlier prophetic communities, despite fewer numbers and weaker equipment, fought with their prophets, suffered wounds and death, yet never weakened or submitted; by patience they gained God's favor, love, and victory, while Muslims scattered in panic over a false report.
rows.anchor: Siz ise yalan haberin yayılmasıyla perişan olup dağıldınız!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb qatele (“fought”) also has a passive reading, qutile, yielding “How many prophets were killed with many Allah-men beside them.”
rows.anchor: “kātele” fiili edilgen olarak “kūtile” şeklinde de okunmuştur.

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur names six prophets killed: Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Isaiah, Zechariah, John, and Hanzala ibn Safwan; the first five were killed by Israelites, Hanzala by Arabs.
rows.anchor: Bunlar İsrâiloğulları’nın öldürdükleri Ermiyâ, Hezekiel, İşâyâ, Zekeriyyâ ve Yahyâ ile Araplar’ın öldürdüğü Hanzale b. Safvân’dır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These prophets were killed in various ways outside battle, yet their followers neither weakened nor submitted; Muslims at Uhud therefore should have shown the same resolve and courage.
rows.anchor: Onlar öldürüldükleri halde beraberlerinde bulunan Allah erleri başlarına gelen musibetten dolayı ne gevşeklik ve zaaf göstermişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Habbab ibn al-Aratt asked the Prophet whether he would pray for relief from the severe harm inflicted by polytheists; the Prophet sensed possible weariness and reluctance to do one's duty, sat upright with a flushed face, and recalled believers tortured with iron combs or sawn in half without abandoning their religion.
rows.anchor: Habbâb b. Eret Hz. Peygamber’e, “Müşriklerden büyük sıkıntı çektik.
